Subject: [UFORL] 'UFOs Shuttering Peace and Quiet'

Courtesy of Pravda - a first for UFORL and as always, you heard
it here first:

UFOS SHUTTERING PEACE AND QUIET

8 April, 2002

At night on Saturday to Sunday, hundreds of citizens of Austria
and Germany (mostly of Bavaria and Baden-Wuertnemberg) were
deprived of their deserved rest. Some unidentified flying objects
disturbed them, which looked like fire balls. As any unexplained
phenomenon, the fire balls excited panic spirits in peaceful
buergers. Austrian citizens even called up the police and
gendarmerie, asking them to take measures against the "sky
disorders." The police many times arrived to the spot, though
there were no tracks of UFO's attack on the Earth. Experts are
difficulty in determining what actually it could have been.

According to them, Austrian and German citizens could have
watched falling fragments of Pegas US carrier rocket, all the
more that earlier NASA notified in advance about possible fall of
the rocket (who knows why, but the story with submerged Mir
station comes to mind), which must take place about April 7.
Though, some scientists suppose this could have been "meteorite
rain," which is a rather usual sight. In Bavarian Centre of Space
Research it was said that the phenomenon was "similar to a
rocket's track. As if something was burning in atmosphere. Though
versions about an UFO or some unknown satellite's explosion soon
fall away. Version of "meteorite rain" is the most probable."

In general, German and Austrian citizens had what to be afraid of
this Sunday. Though, it should be noticed that first week of
April was rich as for space theme. April 3-4, reports appeared
about an UFO approaching to the Earth, which later turned out to
be a meteorite. According to scientists, the meteorite will
collide with the Earth in 800 years. Or, probably, it will not.

Stories about UFOs and meteorites threatening with annihilation
of life in our planet are actively covered by all mass media.
While this is understandable. Stories like that should divert the
public's attention from issues which are most actual for the
world. At least, not only Palestine and Israel should be covered
by the press. Though, as for UFO, mass media should know when to
stop. For, such reports could became as usual as others and stop
drawing the public's attention.
[END]


The Pravda article has links to previous online features,
including the 'Declassifying Project':

5 December, 2001

AMERICAN SCIENTISTS DEMAND TO PUBLISH THE INFORMATION
ABOUT UFO
ACCUMULATED DURING 50 YEARS

A group of American scientists and retired militaries called
"Declassifying Project" launched a campaign for audition of UFO
issue in the US Congress. The members of this group propose to
listen the evidences of extraterrestrial existence. The group
accuses the American government of the attempt to restrict
information about UFO which had been accumulated during the
recent 50 years. Doctor Steven Greer, one of the leaders of
"Declassifying Project" explained why the American government
could hide such information: "During the cold war this
information was secret, because our government did not want the
Soviet Union to obtain admittance to the extraterrestrial
technologies. But the cold war had not ended till now. Our
government is still keeping this information in secret. Probably
there are many projects which conflict with our constitution and
have not been discussed in the Parliament and in the White House.
Maybe the authorities are not ready to admit it." One of the
members of "Declassifying Project", a former military announced,
that he had taken part in a group for investigation of a wrecked
flying saucer where he had found wounded extraterrestrial
astronauts, as BBC reports. According a lady taking part in the
Project, one of the American astronauts who had visited the Moon
told her about the print of an extraterrestrial space ship left
on the ground of this plannet. For the time being there is not
any reaction of the American authorities to the announcements of
the group".
[END]


Another news item which Pravda associates with 'UFOs' is
entitled, 'VALERIAN SOBOLEV ANNOUNCED THE SENSE OF HIS
DISCOVERY'
- see:

http://english.pravda.ru/main/2001/07/24/10865.html
http://english.pravda.ru/society/2001/07/25/10987.html

Although Sobolev's reported claims were widely ridiculed,
interestingly, I note they prompted a response from Jack Shulman
of 'American Computer'. I'm sure some subscribers will recall
Shulman's 1996-98 involvement concerning 'reverse-engineered
alien technology PCs', see for example:

http://byamerican.com/computersolutions/
http://www.american-computer.com/thanksgiving.htm


On 20 August, 2001, Shulman wrote to Pravda:

The above was a very interesting article. Some of my peers
suggested that Dr. Sobolev had access to a UFO and was deploying
reverse engineered Alien technology. Which of course I found a
very clever if humorous interpretation.

I find several exceptions to the announcement in as much as I
have had an opportunity in the past to deploy technology in the
gravity subordination, and transpatial fields, in various
experimentation, and in the development of science in the area of
trans-spatial breakthrough propulsion which also has some
relevance to low cost energy.

I clearly see this announcement not as a challenge, but more as
an invitation by Dr. Sobolev for a wide spectrum of international
collaboration on a scientific and commercial level.

In any event, in spite of language barriers, I'd be interested in
hearing more of what Dr. Sobolev has to say about these
innovations his team and he have alleged to have discovered and
I'll, of course, be glad to reciprocate to the extent I am
allowed, however I would suggest that if a dialog by web is to
occur that both sides be willing to accept the limitations that
the other has on them as to the depth of disclosure, to ensure
that at least some ideas are able to be exchanged academically
and to our both benefit without either of our respective
countries being worried about the possibility of damage to its
respective economic position.

Sincerely yours,

Dr. Jack A. Shulman
CEO / VP Engineering R&D
American computer
Cranford, NY
[END]


Previously, Shulman didn't advocate that the deployment of
reverse-engineered PCs was "a very clever if humorous
interpretation", at least not according to his claims the
transistor had been developed as a result of technology recovered
at Roswell.

These claims were naturally taken seriously by many and Shulman
successfully came across as a businessman who, having innocently
stumbled upon the truth, could be trusted. Here, finally, was
_the evidence_ which proved an alien spaceship crashed at Roswell
and that a grandiose cover-up had been enforced, ever more
despicable than previously imagined.

Shulman's allegations were duly promoted and vehemently defended
on some mailing lists, especially UFO UpDates. Although it was
demonstrated how the transistor's development was consummately
documented and a natural evolution, there was typically no
reasoning with believers.

Alas, like the mythical Roswell flying saucer, it all came
crashing down to earth when it was announced, after some two
years:

Source - IUFO and Riskers Mailing List

ACC Jack Shulman Admits Using UFO's For Bait

On a local radio show in Atlantic City, NJ yesterday, ACC
President Jack Shulman admitted using UFO's, aliens, alien-
abductions, and the paranormal to increase sales for his small NJ
company.

In the interview, Mr. Shulman was asked why this worked. "Because
so many people are involved in this, we have an automatic
audience. They are going to listen to us, because if they don't,
they become part of the conspiracy". Mr. Shulman said he thanks
both the people involved in ufology, and the United States
government for promoting his company for him.

ACC began using this tactic nearly two years ago, when the began
"The Roswell Story." The brainchild of Shulman himself, compiled
of reports from all over the net, in books, and on TV. "People
believe there is something to it, and if we claim that we have
the secrets, they come. While they are there, they might buy a
computer."

Some of those deep in the study of UFO's say that this is
damaging to a cause that is devoted to finding the truth. Shulman
says in response, "..the 'UFO community' is nothing but a bunch
of crackpots and losers, with nothing better to do with their
lives."
[END]
Presumably Shulman, who also professes to have invented the
'Windows' operating system, has a higher opinion of those in the
Russian market place.

Thanks to ananova.com:

Tuesday 9th April 2002

_Meteorite discovery solves German UFO sightings_

A mystery over widespread reports of lights in the sky over
southern Germany has been solved by the discovery of a meteorite.

A Bavarian farmer's wife found a 3ft wide crater in her vegetable
patch with the meteorite lodged at the bottom.

Munich Institute for Geology experts estimate the meteorite
weighed over 100 kilos before hitting the atmosphere at speeds of
almost 125,000mph.

The rock is bigger than a tennis ball but can still be held in
one hand.

It is now at the institute of geology, where officials said it is
worth a lot more than the damage caused to the vegetable patch.

The woman from Friesing took the blackened rock to the local
police station hoping if she reported it she might be eligible
for compensation.

Although her insurance company have told her she is unlikely to
get cash for meteorite damage, she is likely to get a decent
reward from the scientists.

Police in Bavaria and neighbouring Austria were swamped with
calls from worried locals at the weekend. They reported seeing
the sky "lit up like daytime" and hearing a violent explosion.

The farmer's wife said she witnessed bright flashes of light and
heard a loud noise as she put her daughter to bed, but believed
it was youths causing a nuisance.

The Bavarian interior ministry says hundreds of worried people
called to report the UFOs, described as a series of flashes that
looked like lightning.
[END]

The End of the UFO Affair

Tuesday, April 09, 2002
By Ken Layn
FOX NEWS

What happened to the UFOs?
Are the space buddies scared of terrorists?

These important questions were raised (by me) on Monday night, when a
British news site published this report about a strange light in the sky
over southern Germany.
http://www.ananova.com/news/story/sm_562185.html?menu=news.latestheadlines
I realized I hadn't seen a decent flying-saucer story on the wires since
last summer.

It would take minutes of research to prove this, of course. But a dedicated
columnist doesn't mind a little legwork. I searched the news on Yahoo,
Google and BBC. The results clearly support my theory.

Google's news site offered nothing more than that same report from Germany,
a Taipei Times article about a radio station called "UFO," and an
International Herald Tribune feature about April Fools' jokes.

Yahoo News had a single match: an article about a snack food in Hong Kong
called "Nissin UFO Oomori Yaki Soba Instant Noodles."
http://story.news.yahoo.com/news?tmpl=story&u=/nm/20020320/hl_nm/food_additiv
e_1

And this year, the BBC's Web site has published exactly one story about the
space monsters — and it's about a 1950s UFO commission in Britain. (Those
amused by lazy editors will appreciate that this story's photograph
http://news.bbc.co.uk/hi/english/uk/newsid_1740000/1740189.stm
is the same picture used in the last UFO article on the BBC Web site,
http://news.bbc.co.uk/hi/english/uk/newsid_1363000/1363848.stm
from June 2001.)

Forget those stupid Pulitzer prizes. The real Media Scandal is the shocking
lack of reported UFO sightings since Sept. 11.

Is the modern-day space alien so cowardly that it won't visit Earth during
wartime? During World War II, "foo fighters" swarmed around bombers.
http://www.unmuseum.org/foo.htm
During the Cold War,
http://www.coldwar.org/articles/40s/ufo_chrash.php3

the United States went bonkers over UFOs.
http://www.parascope.com/articles/0697/arnold.htm

We've even got astronauts who believe alien spaceships are hanging around
Earth.
http://ufos.about.com/cs/astronautsufos/

Are the ETs afraid of a nutcase like Bin Laden? Aren't the aliens supposed
to be an advanced race? And if so, are they threatened by a guy with bad
kidneys who has to use Hotmail to communicate with his evil minions?

Worse yet, are we bored with the spacemen?

Steven Spielberg gussied up his "E.T." for re-release last month, and the
thing vanished from the multiplex quicker than a Hungarian historical
romance starring Tom Green.
http://news.bbc.co.uk/hi/english/entertainment/film/newsid_1912000/1912954.stm

The X-Files is in its last season, according to news reports.
http://www.eonline.com/News/Items/0,1,9395,00.html

We have to trust the news reports here, because nobody has actually watched
The X-Files in years. They're too busy watching Alias, another hour-long
suspense show with a tough redhead — but it's mercifully free of space
monsters. (Meanwhile, X-Files has become a term
http://story.news.yahoo.com/news?tmpl=story&u=/nm/20020401/od_nm/conspiracy_
dc_1
used to mock the gullible French for buying a conspiracy book claiming a
jet never crashed into the Pentagon.)
http://www.boston.com/dailyglobe2/091/nation/Notion_that_US_staged_attack_on_P
entagon_lures_France+.shtml


The Weekly World News used to report on presidents shaking hands with
extraterrestrials.
http://weeklyworldnews.com/features/aliens_story.cfm?instanceid=12068
Now we get AP photos of Laura Bush being embraced by a guy in a rabbit suit.


Some egghead will probably write an article about this for an academic
journal in the fall of 2002. So what? Thanks to the magic of the Internet,
I can say it right now: the Great Alien-American Love Affair is over.
Sorry, Commander Xamfrangle, but I sort of met this other entity ... and,
well, this hurts me more than it hurts you. And you'll always be very
special to me, but ... I need to see other species right now. Maybe
someday, if you could, like, stop being so noncommittal and take a little
more responsibility and maybe appear in daylight ... I don't know. I'm just
confused. I need space. And I need you to go back to space.

Surely I'll get a lot of e-mail about this controversial statement. But I'm
ready to defend the position.

The big Star Wars show at the Brooklyn Museum of Art?
http://www.brooklynart.org/visit/special_exhibitions/starwars/Default.htm
Simple nostalgia for the good old days of gas lines, Jimmy Carter and
friendly wookies. The new robot dogs from Sanyo? A practical solution for
apartment dwellers scared of real-life killer dogs. These troubling
Japanese space-alien commercials
http://newtown.hi-ho.ne.jp/raibo/raidersei/image/agency/cm/mail.swf
for an Internet service? Could mean anything.
http://www.thismodernworld.com/weblog/archive/2002_04_07_bloggera.html#75162

10.04.2002

'Outback rail dream arrives after century '
By GREG ANSLEY in Canberra

With UFOs streaking in the night sky above and politicians
slugging it out below, the first tracks have finally been laid
for a railway line that will follow the trail of 19th century
Afghan camel-drivers.

How else could the Alice Springs to Darwin line be launched, a
century or so after political campaigners first began their
regular election-time promises to send trains across some of the
world's most inhospitable country?

begun humping 155,000 tonnes of steel over 1410km of Australia's

cigar- and hat-shaped objects whipping through the night.

Subject: [UFORL] Galaxy 'may hold Earth-like planets'

Courtesy of BBC online:

Wednesday, 10 April, 2002

The search for life in outer space has received a boost.

British scientists say that in theory there could be a billion
Earth-like planets in our own galaxy, the Milky Way.

It may be only a matter of time before telescopes spot them.

The prediction has been made by two astronomers at the Open
University using a mathematical model.

According to computer simulations, some of the newly discovered
distant Solar Systems should contain smaller, Earth-like planets.

"We do know that there are a lot of known planetary systems
beyond our own Solar System," Dr Barrie Jones told the BBC.

"But what we don't know is if there are any Earth-like planets up
there."


_Gaseous giants_

Astronomers have identified nearly 100 planets in orbit around
distant stars.

These so-called "exoplanets" are not the sort that could support
life. They are enormous and of the same gaseous make-up as
Jupiter.

Dr Jones believes that smaller Earth-like planets may exist in
some of these far-flung planetary systems.

"What I've been doing is saying: 'Well we can't see Earths yet -
but let's suppose that they are there - could they actually exist
or would they be flung out into interstellar space by the
presence of these big giants?'" he said.

He said a computer model to see whether Earth-like planets could
survive among the giants had produced "some rather encouraging
results".
_Ursae Majoris_

It suggests that more than one billion habitable planets could
exist in our own galaxy.

Dr Jones said it would be 10-15 years before telescopes are
powerful enough to spot any smaller planets that might be
present. But astronomers will at least know where to look.

The Solar System most like ours discovered so far is centred
around a distant star called 47 Ursae Majoris.

Two planets orbit the star - one twice the size of Jupiter and
the other slightly smaller.

The findings will be presented at the National Astronomy Meeting
in Bristol on Wednesday 10 April.
[END]

'The salient point to observe is that the objects
are first seen at a point essentially just outside
the city limits of Seattle, the most populous city

indicate the objects are fairly impressive in size
especially if one accepts the statement that the
initial flash lit up Arnold's "whole aircraft, even
the cockpit." (Proceedings, p. 19) How could such
a large fleet of supersonic objects not be seen and
especially heard by large numbers of people in this

Second, the presumption of all the UFO (let's not be

has been that when Arnold turned his plane to get a
better gander (ho ho) at The Nine (an interesting

he turned to starboard, since he was sitting in the

face the sun. My idle speculation is that he turned
to port, ie north. This would have given him additional
shade and improved his sight picture -- as turning
to the south would not -- despite it being against
the direction of The Nine. It is surprising that someone
whose expertise is in optics would not have thought
of this. Or is it? Anyway, there is a 50 per cent
chance that Arnold did turn to port, which taken
together with the other pelicanist evidence would
weight the evidence in favour of birds. Or even
pelicans.

Which version of Arnold's story do you want to begin with - you

Source: 'The Coming of the Saucers'


The first story is of merely observing objects crossing the face

Subject: [UFORL] 'To Chinese UFO buffs, it's a serious science'

Courtesy of CNN:

April 12, 2002

CNN's Kristie Lu Stout

HONG KONG, China (CNN) -- UFO research is the stuff of sci-fi
buffs and conspiracy freaks, but in China it's treated seriously.

Joseph Wong, a lab manager at Hong Kong's City University, is a
man of science. His job is to assess the structural performance
of buildings.

But familiar as he is with hard data, Wong is also a fan of the
unexplained.

"If something flies over, there's a very good reason for trying
to understand why they're here, why they come to us, what is
their relationship between us and them," he says.

Wong is the Chairman of Hong Kong's thriving UFO club --
exploring "unidentified flying objects" or, to the uninitiated,
"flying saucers."

The club meets once a month to explore otherworldly topics like
"E.T. Civilization" and "Alien Kung Fu."

Members occasionally meet at a cyber cafe called UFO Station in
Hong Kong's Tsim Sha Tsui district. The spot is home to Hong
Kong's own version of the X-files.

The dark monitor-lit café has UFO books, newsletters, and old
news clippings of close encounters -- material that UFO club
members take very seriously.

_A masters in UFOlogy?_

"In order to understand UFO phenomena, we need to have a broad
understanding of different disciplines," says Albert So,
university professor and Hong Kong UFO club member, "including
mathematics, physics, history, philosophy, even some sort of
paranormal activities and all that."

Hong Kong's UFO enthusiasts, like So, are not dreamy stargazers,
but researchers who see their passion as a science.
So much so that they're lobbying for a university degree program
in "UFOlogy."

"The graduates of this program will grasp at least all the major
knowledge in order to understand UFO phenomena, and also other
technologies and any skills related to UFOs," says So.

"After students or friends finish this degree, they may have
their own understanding about this universe," Wong adds.

"Maybe they will be able to come up with a new universe model,
new way of life, or whatever."

It sounds like a tough sell, but it may not be hard to pitch in
mainland China, where there is little taboo about discs that glow
in the night or theories on visitors from out there.

_Flying boats in China_

China's state-run media reports on UFO sightings. Even the
government's Ministry of Science and Technology treats the topic
with respect.

"It seems that people in the East are more open to discuss issues
related to UFOs," So says.

"Perhaps that is something to do with the culture of the races.
In particular, Chinese. Chinese is a kind of race who easily
believes in something supernatural."

And they may have been believing for a long time. UFO researchers
point to an ancient drawing of the 100-year story of an emperor
meeting a flying boat - a compelling artifact in support of UFO
study, but not the only one.

"For me, it's not very important whether there is really a UFO
that can fly or not," Wong says.

"It's when we are investigating this, I think it's the process
that actually helps us to understand more about ourselves or our
planet."

For club chairman Joseph Wong, the truth may be out there, but
the payoff is personal - studying aliens helps to satiate a very
healthy, and very human, curiosity.
[END]

20th - 21st, 2002.<BR>
<BR>
<A HREF="http://melbourneufo.com/">http://melbourneufo.com/</A><BR>
<BR>
In a last minute collapse and change to a one day<BR>
event, it has been called off!<BR>
<BR>
The original idea came from a Mr Craig McDonough &amp;<BR>
Mr Lyndon Reeks at Big Organised Productions.<BR>
<BR>
<A HREF="www.iholidays.com">www.iholidays.com</A><BR>
<BR>
Located at 157 High Street, Prahran, VICTORIA 3181,<BR>
AUSTRALIA &lt;lyndon_bop@atlasmail.com&gt;. But McDonough<BR>
&amp; Reeks have created some angry emails between<BR>
some researchers down this way.<BR>
<BR>
Ten months ago the original dream had a high<BR>
quality roll call:<BR>
<BR>
GRAHAM BIRDSALL (UK), GEORGINA BRUNI (UK),<BR>
DR. RICHARD HAINES (USA), DR. JOHN MACK (USA),<BR>
BUD HOPKINS (USA), JOHN AUCHETTL (AUST),<BR>
GEORGE SIMPSON (AUST), MIKE FARRELL (AUST).<BR>
<BR>
However, when the final list came out the big guns<BR>
were all missing, and another list was posted on the<BR>
web page.<BR>
<BR>
By February 2002 the speakers list was reduced to:<BR>
<BR>
GRAHAM BIRDSALL (UK), CHRISTOPHER MARTIN (UK),<BR>
NICK REDFERN (UK), JIM MARRS (USA), HARRY MASON (AUST),<BR>
GEORGE SIMPSON (AUST), MIKE FARRELL (AUST),<BR>
BRENDA BUTLER (AUST).<BR>
<BR>
But NICK REDFERN (UK) was not a real runner and was<BR>
soon replaced by BILL CHALKER (AUST).<BR>
<BR>
Things went from bad to worse as speakers became agitated<BR>
with the lack of communication. Thanks to the good<BR>
common sense of a Mr Mike Farrell, some hard questions<BR>
were asked about the organisation in a Farrell "REALITY<BR>
CHECK" email.<BR>
<BR>
Before long, Mr Farrell (a well respected researcher<BR>
from New South Wales) pulled the pin on his speakers<BR>
agreement. He cited many errors in the production and<BR>
tried to get someone to listen in, his concerns were with<BR>
the paying public and their expectations. Then came the<BR>
crunch when the organisers reported that around 50 prepaid<BR>
tickets had only been sold! That was it, the end came<BR>
quickly as the others followed and bailed out.<BR>
<BR>
The Australian Skeptics report - When asked what went<BR>
wrong the organisers said that it was due to some<BR>
malcontents who killed it off. A more detailed case<BR>
was not given. However, a Mr George Simpson was singled<BR>
out as one of the loose cannons, that lacked guts and<BR>
that killed the dream.<BR>
<BR>
They also reported that well known Victorian and one of<BR>
Australia's few respected senior researchers into the<BR>
paranormal, did not even get off the 'starting blocks' with<BR>
the organisers, back in August 2001, when he was asked<BR>
to help and also speak. Mr John Auchettl of <I>Phenomena<BR>
Research Australia (PRA)</I> is reported to have questioned<BR>
the lack of any solid plans, especially in the advertising<BR>
of the conference.<BR>
<BR>
Auchettl noted to other researchers that the venue was<BR>
too large for a two day conference. The '<I>Dallas Brooks Hall</I>'<BR>
can hold 1700 people and was too big for such an audience,<BR>
as well as that the place lacked food or transport access.<BR>
Auchettl at another conference this year at Melbourne<BR>
University is reported to have said that he could fill<BR>
around 100 to 300 seats top, so it would be a very empty<BR>
hall for a very long time. He asked if the venue could be<BR>
moved to a hotel conference room that speakers could rest<BR>
in their rooms before their talks and have something to eat,<BR>
then it would work. Also the public could book in at their<BR>
own rooms and rest when they needed. But that fell on deaf<BR>
ears. So back in Aug 2001, Auchettls reported that he<BR>
would have to declined the invitation and wished them all<BR>
the luck in the world. As it turned out they needed it.<BR>

Were aliens about to invade Britain shortly after the
Second World War? R.A.F. pilots reported strange

unidentified flying objhects in the literal sense of the term,

David Clarke and Andy Roberts

interested but this programme reveals details of secret
investigations carried out by a government terrified of
the Russians.

John

Those recollections by Chuck Dalldorf were up on the Woodbridge website
www.woodbridgeweb.co.uk a couple of years ago. In some circles on the twin
bases the rumours were flying around. I think it depended on who you knew,
and which Flight you were on. I met with Tim Egercic last weekend and
dicussed just this point - in the Security Police, people from one Flight
could be on base with people on another Flight for years and not even know
each other's names.

People in the know were ordered to keep quiet, or at least it was suggested
to some that they keep quiet. There are perfectly mundane reasons why this
might have been done, e.g. to preserve the reputation of the USAF, maintain
morale, and to stop gangs of personnel from making the forest their second
home. In Sky Crash it is related that in late Feb 1981, signs had been
posted at the roads leading into the forest stating that permission of the
Base Commander was needed to enter the forest. So they did put put a lid on
it, for whatever reason.

Robert

From: "David Clarke" <cd292@crazydiamonds.fsnet.co.uk>
Date: Sat, 20 Apr 2002 11:33:58 +0100
Subject: Re: [UFORL] Bentwaters/Woodbridge UFOs

Greetings list,

During my research into the 'classic' Bentwaters-Lakenheath radar UFO
event of 1956, I've traced a number of former RAF and USAF personnel.
One in particular, a pilot who flew with the USAF 512th FIS based at
Bentwaters in 1955-57, was directly involved in the 'search' for the
radar UFOs and has some very interesting comments on light phenomena
produced by unusual weather conditions on the twin-base complex.
His comments may be a highly significant clue towards the nature
of the lights seen in Rendlesham Forest in 1980.

He writes:

"The UFO became a very familiar event for us at Bentwaters during our three
year
assignment there. I have a pretty good memory of a number of UFO sightings
and of trying to chase one night. We really were a bit disturbed about some
of the things we sighted until the sightings were explained. I will relate a
couple of the more significant events to you and you can judge for yourself
what we concluded.

    Bentwaters AFB had UFO sightings that really kept us excited for weeks
in 1956. The event that really started the whole thing consisted of a phone
call from the tower operator asking us to take a look at the strange lights
that were "floating" on front of the tower. It was early evening and there
were only a few of the pilots in the ready room so we all ran out to the
tower to see what was happening. I have to say that there were strange
glowing balls of light floating in front of the tower. They would float
slowly by the tower and then seem to ascend slowly to about 500 feet and
cease to be visible. As we stood there we next saw some more light balls
floating down the runway from the North end of the runway and do the same
thing. We watched this happen for perhaps 20 minutes. It was very easy to
let yourself get pretty excited and so we called our GCA and asked them if
they say anything. My memory says that they could not find anything on their
screens but that they did sight them when they went outside . Their view
point was from the East side of the runway slightly to the South of the
tower. We were all dumbfounded by this activity. After about 20 minutes the
frequency of sightings seemed to decrease to a point of none for 15 minutes
and then two balls would appear and do the same thing. After standing in the
chill evening air we finally retired to the O Club for a few drinks and talk
about what we had seen.

   At this point I should relate the weather conditions. It was cool and
very damp with a light fog in the air. The night was clear of clouds.

   This strange happening was seen on several nights during the next few
weeks. Always the same direction and pattern seemed to be the order of
things. Some times there were a lot of sightings and other times only a very
few. Spooky to say the least.

    The conclusion reached for this series of UFO events came about a few
weeks later when I just happened to mention the subject to my landlord who
had a family estate about four miles from Bentwaters. He said, "oh yes,
these lights have been seen many times over the years and long before you
came, even during the war and perhaps before." At this point he stated that
" these lights only happen during periods of damp slightly foggy weather.
They are caused by autos following the road way that runs almost straight at
the runway and then turns to the West about a quarter mile from the runway."
.... "The cause was determined to be auto lights on approaching machines
being somehow reflected by a layers of cold damp air that lay over the area
of the airbase as a low altitude." Sounded like a winner to me so we tested
the theory and guess what, that was the source of the UFOs.

   Testing was easy but it was not easy to find the proper conditions and
we waited a long time to get a sighting that would allow us to test. When
the time arrived we drove down the road toward the runway while observers
were standing around the tower. As we descended the high ground North of the
runway we would turn the lights off and on for a distance of about a half
mile just before the road turned West. Yep, you guessed it. The observers
say our lights blink off and on but only by watching the floating balls of
light as they drifted by. That was enough for me to say the we had found the
source of our "Bentwaters UFOs".

    There was [another] event that occurred early one evening some time
doing
this period of sightings. It consisted of a strange bright light that seemed
to be directly East of the Base and was acting sort of oddly. I scrambled in
an F-86 and went out over the North Sea chasing it. I used afterburner in
the climb and the "thing" just ran off and left me. As I broke out of a
layer of poor visibility at about 25,000 feet I finally got my mind to see
what was really out there and make the decision that there was no way to
ever catch up. It was a nice big star that sure had me going for a few
minutes. At about 30,000 feet I reported the star and came home. Just goes
to show you that you can really get fooled visually by lights that are
effected by water vapor in layers of air. I felt a bit foolish after I
returned from that one.

   There you have the information of the only UFO sightings that I know of
during 1954 through 1957. I suspect that there have been many others who
thought they were being attacked by strange flying objects that moved in
impossible ways at impossible velocities.

That is about it for my part of the Bentwaters UFO adventure. I and my
fellow pilots in our squadron were all specially trained for night weather
intercepts and so we were all quite competent in such situations. I have
seen some really frightening things while in the air but in every case I was
able to eventually rationalize what I saw and know that it was just ground
light or other aircraft doing a number on me. After many years of flying and
viewing strange lights in the sky I can state that there has never been a
happening that I could believe was not natural earth bound source light. I
would love to see some real UFOs but have given up for the duration."

Courtesy of ananova.com:

_Expert claims Bavarian meteorite announcement was wrong_

A German scientist claims a supposed meteorite found after
strange lights were seen over Germany is just an ordinary rock.

The tennis ball-sized object was thought to be evidence of a
meteor strike in Bavaria.

But Dieter Heinlein says it was just slag material which is
common in the region.

However, he is sure meteorites did fall in the region that night
and is now searching for the evidence.

A farmer's wife said she found the rock in a 3ft wide crater in
her vegetable patch.

Officials from Munich's Institute for Geology told the media it
was a meteorite.

Dieter told Ananova: "I have seen about two dozen specimens which
have been brought by people who thought they had found meteorites
but no real meteorites have been found yet. It is not easy to
search for meteorites but we are hopeful."

He has spent 25 years studying and collecting space rocks and has
worked for Germany's space and aeronautics agency - the DLR.

Dieter is now locating the area in the Alpine foothills most
likely to have been hit by the meteorites. He said: "They are
interesting because they are extraterrestrial matter which can
tell us more about the origins of our solar system."

Dieter hopes to measure the radioactivity in the rocks, he said:
"The sooner we find them the better chance we have of measuring
the short-lived isotopes present in them."

Subject: [UFORL] 'Would you believe?'

Courtesy of National Post Online:

Would you believe?

Callers to Art Bell's radio show get genial tolerance for their
creepy tales

Robert Fulford
National Post

It was the middle of the night, as it always is, and Jim in
Wolfville was on the line, calling all the way from Nova Scotia
to Art Bell's home radio studio in Pahrump, Nev. (pop. 7,400),
where Jim's and Art's voices were being beamed up to a satellite
so they could be sent back down to about 500 radio stations
across the United States and Canada.

Jim is one of us, one of 10 million or so listeners (occasional,
frequent or obsessive) to the most outlandish long-running radio
show anywhere, Cross Country with Art Bell, a five-hour program
much loved by night workers, insomniacs and those who enjoy
visiting the outer reaches of human credibility.

Bell may be the only broadcaster in the business who will never
scoff at you when aliens land their ship in your backyard. He
won't think you odd if you yearn for yet one more discussion of
the famous 1957 Chevrolet that "just fell out of the sky" some
years ago in Long Beach, Calif. On his show a typical caller
begins, "I'm phoning about the stories about mysterious balls of
light."

Jim was calling from Wolfville because he was bothered by some
ghost voices, messages from the Beyond, that Art's guests of the
evening had taped in graveyards and were now playing on the air.
The spirits on the tapes said nothing interesting, of course.
Like all dead people ever contacted by spiritualists, they
apparently thought that just getting in touch was enough, like
remembering to phone your Mom on Sunday. They certainly didn't
feel called upon to communicate anything they had learned on the
Other Side.

But Jim wasn't concerned about that. He was worried because he
had distinctly heard the ghosts on the tapes ... breathing. As he
said, "It is kind of interesting that the ghosts have to breathe.
If that's the case, do they eat?"
I suspect Jim was a skeptic pretending to be innocent, but Bell
took him seriously. He treats unbelievers and believers with the
same genial tolerance. "Good point," he said. "After all, they're
dead. What do they need with breathing sounds?"

One of the tape-collecting spiritualists was ready for that
question. "To be honest," he answered, "I really don't believe
they are actually breathing. I think it's a memory thing. They're
remembering how they talked in life, and to do that, they had to
breathe. That's how they communicate with us." Bell, who has been
hearing creative explanations like that for more than two
decades, pronounced this one good, in fact perfect. His voice
conveyed his warm appreciation of a sure-footed researcher.

Bell himself is an object of curiosity to many listeners. Who is
he, and does he believe what all those people tell him? He was
born in 1945, to a father and mother who were both U.S. Marines.
He worked as an operator in radio stations and finally landed an
on-air job. He specialized in unexplained phenomena, from UFOs to
spontaneous human combustion, because he realized no one else was
mining those subjects. Now he sometimes limits callers to one
topic ---- he'll open a specific phone line for, say, vampires,
or time travellers.

His listeners' stories often sound true to him. He believes
spaceships visit Earth, and thinks he's seen one. He takes a
friendly interest in all the people who phone, whether he agrees
with them or not.

"I help them tell their story and let the audience judge. I don't
laugh at them. I listen." No one screens the calls.

The tales that come to life on Bell's show range from the
eccentric to the downright creepy. The second category includes
the Hale-Bopp comet in 1997. It was on Bell's show that someone
first reported an alien spaceship was shadowing Hale-Bopp in the
general direction of Earth. The rumour spread, and 39 members of
Heaven's Gate, a California cult, killed themselves in the belief
that the spaceship would take them to a better place.

Bell's fans don't blame Bell: He carried debunking material about
the story as well as the story itself, and in any case the
cultists had been waiting for a sign. They might just as easily
have found it in the words of Stairway to Heaven.

In Austin, Milwaukee, Orange County and other places, Art Bell
chat clubs have sprung up so people can get together and talk
about what they've heard on his show. His listeners love to
figure the angles on whatever phenomenon comes up. One of his
callers, after hearing a program on people who died during
operations and then came back to life, demanded to know why these
were called "near-death experiences" when all the signs indicated
the patients were in fact dead. Proudly, this caller announced
that he'd worked out the answer: Insurance companies don't want
to pay death benefits to the same person more than once.

Then there was the man who phoned to express his concern about
cloning and criminal justice. Won't cloning mean that a person's
DNA will be no longer be unique and therefore won't be admissible
as evidence in criminal cases? Bell replied, "That is really an
awfully good point. If you had a bunch of clones and there was a
murder, you'd have no way of separating the suspects ... There
would be no DNA evidence that would stand up in court." That sort
of question would occur only to a Bell fan.

Stephen Osborne, the editor of Geist magazine in Vancouver, told
me a few years ago that I should listen to Bell. Osborne
occasionally passes on details of callers I've missed, such as
the man who hit a 700-pound Sasquatch on a road in the Midwest
last summer. He had moved it, with jeep and winch, to what he
called his "Y2K-fallout shelter," and it seemed still to be
alive. He wanted Bell himself to take charge of it. He didn't
trust anyone else. Bell advised him to call a vet and promised to
put him in touch with a Sasquatch expert. In Bell's world it is
taken for granted that there's an expert on everything, whether
the thing itself exists or not.
[END]

http://www.nationalpost.com/commentary/columnists/story.html?f=/s
tories/20020416/652746.html

 Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2002 00:46:43 +0200
 From: "Pavel Spurny" <spurny@asu.cas.cz>
 Subject: EN060402 bolide

Dear all,

I am sending you the information about the results on the
EN060402 bolide which was observed by many people over a large
teritorry of Central Europe. As you can read below, it was a
really exceptional case.

The April 6, 2002 fireball

A very bright fireball illuminated large territory of Western Austria
and Southern Bavaria on Saturday evening, April 6 at 22:20:18
local time (UT+2h). The fireball was observed by many casual
witnesses over the territory of almost whole Central Europe, but
most observations were reported from Bavaria and Western
Austria. Except of numerous visual observations, the fireball
was recorded by several kinds of scientific instruments. The
most important records were obtained by the systematic long-term
observational photographic program - the European Fireball
Network (EN). The records were taken at 5 German, one Czech and
one Austrian station of the EN. Each of these stations is
equipped with one all-sky camera, which is open whole night and
whole sky is photographed on one image. The German and Austrian
stations are equipped with mirror all-sky cameras and are
operated by the German Aerospace Center DLR, Berlin. The Czech
stations of the EN are equipped with very precise Zeiss Distagon
fish-eye objectives and are operated by the Astronomical
Institute of the Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic,
Ondrejov. Most Czech stations had cloudy skies on April 6,
however. The photographic records are most important for exact
determination of the fireball atmospheric trajectory, including
prediction of meteorite impact area and derivation of
heliocentric orbit. In addition to these photographic data, the
fireball was recorded by three radiometric systems placed in the
Czech Republic at Ondrejov Observatory and Kunzak station, which
gives us basic information about light curve and maximum
brightness of the fireball and about exact time of the event.
Furthermore the fireball was recorded by at least at two
infrasound stations, one located at Freyung, Germany
(see http://www.seismologie.bgr.de) and second at Deelen,
The Netherlands (see
http://www.knmi.nl/~evers/infrasound/events/020406/bavaria-bolide.html )
and also at several seismic stations from Austria,
Southern Germany and Switzerland.

All data presented below are based only on above-mentioned
photographic and radiometric data recorded within the EN
observing program and are very close to final values. All
records were measured, reduced and all computations were
performed at the Ondrejov Observatory, the headquarters of the
European Fireball Network.

The fireball started its almost 92 km long luminous trajectory
at an altitude of 85.6 km about 15 km NE from Innsbruck, Austria
(longitude 11.564 deg E, latitude 47.304 deg N). Maximum
brightness of about -18 absolute magnitude was reached in a
bright flare at a height of 21 km near Garmisch-Partenkirchen,
Germany (longitude 10.91 deg E, latitude 47.51 deg N). The
fireball terminated at an altitude of only 15.8 km about 20 km W
from Ga-Pa (longitude 10.85 deg E, latitude 47.53 deg N). Such
deep penetration of a fireball is very scarce and this fireball
belongs to the deepest ever-photographed fireballs in the
history. It also implicates, that some part of the initial mass
survived the ablation processes in the atmosphere and landed on
the ground as meteorites. The slope of the atmospheric
trajectory to the Earth's surface was 49.5 degrees. The fireball
entered the atmosphere with the velocity of 20.9 km/s and during
its flight substantially decelerated to the final value of only
4 km/s, when ablation process was stopped. According to the
dynamic behavior in the atmosphere this fireball belongs to the
fireball type I, which is usually identified with stony
material, mostly ordinary chondrites. The initial dynamic mass
of the entering meteoroid was about 500 kg and most of this mass
was ablated and only about 30 kg of total mass could land on the
ground in several fragments. The impact area is relatively
large, it is at least several kilometers long and about 1km
wide. The main fragments will lie eastwards from Schwangau,
Germany. Smaller fragments could be found also around the
Austria-Germany border westwards from Ga-Pa. The whole area is
located in high mountains (the Alps), which is unfortunately
very unfavorable for any systematic search.

Subject: [UFORL] 'Green goo conjures up alien theory'

The Associated Press
4/22/02 10:15 PM

VERBENA, Ala. (AP) -- The eerie green glow emanating at night
from a field had folks in Chilton County wondering whether aliens
chose Alabama as a landing ground or grave site.

The green light was seen March 16 in a 100-foot by 75-foot field
off Chilton County Road 59.

"It was plumb weird looking," said Rodney McGuire. "I'm 54 years
old and I've lived in Chilton County all my life and I've never
seen anything like it."

McGuire called for backup and asked Bill Collum, director of the
Chilton County Emergency Management Office, to take a look.

"When Rodney called me he said 'There is green stuff all over
this field and it's glowing,"' Collum said. "Rodney said, 'You
better bring your Geiger counter. It might be radioactive."'

Not to worry -- an extra-terrestrial invasion isn't on the way,
and the Geiger counter showed no evidence of radiation.

The mystery was solved by Chilton County Extension Agent Gary
Gray, who said the green substance was actually a glowing fungus
that grows on decaying wood. It has been known variously as fox
fire, will-o-the-wisp, cold fire and faerie fire.

Sandy Wimberley, whose parents own the field, said the fungus
grew on stumps and limbs left after her parents cleared the land.

"We were just amazed to see something glowing in the dark like
that," Wimberley said.
[END]

Dave, your posting has reminded me of another, contemporary
testimony which seems worthwhile recalling.

I have highlighted the details previously, however, it was so
long ago that I can't remember where and when. It may only have
been in private discussions and never before revealed publicly,
until now.

The story comes from Roy Dent and I first heard of it from Jean-
Pierre Pharabod, who, appreciating my undoubted interest,
thoughtfully obtained Roy's permission that I might pursue this
further directly with Roy.

Jean-Pierre clarified:

"I think you will be interested in knowing that in 1956, there
had probably been another kind of Lakenheath incident over Great-
Britain.

This case has just been unveiled in the skeptic discussion group.
Of course it could be a hoax, but from the general discussion on
skeptic it think it's unlikely. Roy Dent agreed that I pass on
this case to you. Up to now he thought he could not speak of this
because of the British Official Secrets Act".

During April, 1996, Roy had initially commented on a well-known
Skeptics mailing list:

I'm not aware of what qualifies Tony Mills to comment on the
performance of radar in the 1950's - I assume that he is
referring to the incident quoted briefly below in this posting -
but my excuse is that I was a radar operator with the RAF in
Norfolk during the period in question.

Although it is true that radar had not reached today's level of
sophistication, it was quite definitely far superior to what Mr
Mills would have us believe, and was perfectly capable of
tracking *conventional aircraft of the period* with a claimed
accuracy in range and bearing of less than 100 yards (if my
memory serves me correctly). It is true that height information
was much less reliable.

The 1956 incident which I witnessed was not at night, it was
during the afternoon, but was certainly sometime during the
summer and pre-Suez. The objects, which caused a *major* 'flap',
certainly came into UK air space over the North Sea, but
initially from a northerly direction. At that time this was the
favoured direction for a sneak attack on the UK by the Soviet
Union. I cannot remember the height, suffice to say that I
remember it as being well above the operational ceiling of RAF
fighter at that time. As I said above height information was not
as accurate as range and bearing. What was amazing was the speed
at which these things moved. After forty odd years I cannot
remember an exact figure, but one could get a rough idea of speed
by noting the distance between the traces of the targets produced
by successive scans of the radar head. Instead of the modest
little jumps that even experimental aircraft such as the P1
(later the Lightning) took, these things leapt across the
screens. Fighter aircraft were scrambled eventually (mainly
Javelins I think) from bases around the UK as these targets
proceeded to make a Grand Tour of Britain. They "flew" so high
and so fast that none of our aircraft could get anywhere near
them. Eventually the disappeared somewhere over the Atlantic I
think, they certainly went out of radar range.

During this chase, I was able to hear what amounted to a running
commentary from other stations in the RAF's chain of air defence
radar stations around the country, plus some comments via vhf
radio from the fighter pilots. Dozens of aircraft and their crews
were involved, scores of radar operators and Air Defence staff
knew/heard/saw what was happening. And yet, to the best of my
knowledge, this incident never got reported publicly. I wonder
how many similar events there have been over the years?

To this day I do not know what I witnessed, I have kept a
completely open mind on it, but I am still very intrigued....
I will be watching the BBC2 TV program with great interest, I
will reserve *my* judgement on it until I have seen it.
[END OF COMMENTS]


The BBC2 TV program referred to was Jenny's feature on the
Lakenheath case.

In our subsequent discussions, Roy confirmed:

I watched Jenny Randles' program with great interest,
particularly the events over Norfolk and Suffolk. I have to say
that the incident I witnessed was quite definitely not the same
one as in that program, although there were distinct
similarities.

What I observed certainly happened in the same year, it was
sometime during the summer, I regret that I cannot be precise
with dates after all this time, but it was certainly in the
period between noon and 16.00. To answer another of your
questions, I was stationed at that time at RAF Trimmingham, which
was on the Norfolk coast a few miles from Cromer, and just
outside the village of Mundesley. We were mainly operating as
part of the UK's Air Defence Radar chain which consisted of
ourselves, RAF Buchan in Scotland, Ventnor on the Isle of Wight,
and possibly one or more similar stations further west in the UK,
but I simply cannot now remember. There was also a similar
station at RAF Neatished, which I believe is still operational,
which had similar equipment but which operated only 'during
office hours'.

Neatishead was at the time our Sector, to whom we directly
reported. Trimmingham operated twenty four hours a day, and after
midnight we were usually the only station of our type
operational. At those times, the area for which we were
responsible included all of the UK, plus much of Northern Europe,
and extended deep into Eastern Germany.

On the afternoon in question, I was acting junior N.C.O for our
watch ('B' Watch if I recall correctly) although my substantive
rank was only SAC. There would also have been, beside a crew of
about twelve other ranks, a Senior N.C.O (Sergeant or Flight
Sergeant) plus the Officer of the Watch a Flying Officer. We
worked a rather peculiar twenty four hour watch system which
meant that on that day we were on duty between 12.00 Noon and
16.00, then again that same midnight until 08.00 the next
morning. I am therefore able to be fairly precise with the time,
if not the date. That afternoon my task was to monitor the direct
landlines which connected us to all the other stations in the
chain, maintain our log book (I wonder if these and other logs
still exist?) and keep a general watch on what was being plotted
on our table. Obviously when any unusual or unidentified "raid" -
that was the term we used - was plotted, the Senior N.C.O and
Officer of the Watch would be alerted. In fairness they would
usually spot oddities before we did!

Because of my task that day, I was able to hear what all the
other stations in the chain was seeing - I could hear their
plotters directly - and I was also able, by means of my patch
panel, to plug into and legitimately listen to conversations
between GCI controllers on the ground, and the fighter aircraft
which they were attempting to vector onto their targets. There
were thus *at least* a hundred or more (I would estimate)
witnesses to the event, both on the ground and in the air. *All*
the ops. rooms would have been keeping logs of the events as I
was.

Additionally, and I do not believe this is generally appreciated
now, all stations of our type routinely took photographs of the
radar display on film every 15 seconds. This film could then be
projected onto plotting tables etc. for display. This animated
film was also used from time to time for practice/training
purposes. This film was kept, unusual events would be kept in
this way indefinitely. I suggest that film of radar screens
recording this, and perhaps similar events, is almost certainly
still in existence somewhere in either the MOD or Public Records
Office. I wonder if researchers have ever asked to see this kind
of evidence? In Jenny Randles fascinating BBC2 program we saw her
examining lots of paper files, we saw what looked like routine
library clips of rocket launches, but no mention of radar film.

Final note, the radar equipment mainly involved (as far as I'm
aware) was Marconi Type 80 (long distance surveillance radar) and
Type 13 (I don't know the maker) for information on altitude.
[END]

I am entitled to expect that Bennett understands the fundamentals

It was never my "idea" that Arnold possibly observed a squadron

My 'idea' was a logical conclusion that those nine objects in
formation, presupposing they were not alien spaceships [the most

previous investigations seemed to have ruled out aircraft being
responsible, an obvious research undertaking was to contact

attributes described by Arnold were recognised by them.

offering the exact same conclusion - an undulating,
intermittently 'fluttering and gliding', echelon formation was a
distinctive characteristic of American White Pelicans, indigenous
to Washington state.

So far as 'flying saucers from outer space' and due skepticism
are concerned, the onus is on believers to provide some tangible
evidence - an elementary criteria which hasn't been satisfied in
over FIFTY years of fervent endeavours.

As that will evidently never happen, they are often merely
reduced to bewailing their woes.

somehow remains that science and the media do not have sufficient
intellectual capacity to accept the alien visitation evidence in
front of them.

multiplying scores of genuine Government documents which

reliable, regressive hypnotherapy.

It's so overwhelming that people are stupid if they can't see
this.

most of them blatantly bogus, then the opposite must equally be
true.

inevitably exposed as quite the reverse and confirmation merely
of being gullible.

It's not so long ago since Michael Hesemann chided me:

"I saw the tent footage many times and just the speed of the
movements and also the sharpness of the images indicates it was
shot with a 16 mm camera and not with video. The only reason why
Ray doesn't like it is that it is so bloody dark (dimly lit) and
looks pathetically bad. I personally think it shows the being
when the medics try to remove its spacesuit. A tent in the desert
at night... with no electricity, that's why it is so dark. But
all these sceptics will say again: Look, they have something to
hide, looks, why is it so bad...".

Michael is seemingly undeterred that the 'tent footage' was
subsequently proven to have been filmed with a colour video
camera in a Bedfordshire barn, starring the local butcher as
Hesemann's medic and the farmer as President Truman.

Someone mentioned to me that Hesemann recently wrote to 'UFO
Updates', avowing, "Regarding my alleged 'gullibility' I am one
of the very few UFO researchers who try to find the truth 'out
there', by extensive field investigations in 44 countries of the
world. I think I work too hard and too carefully to be 'easily
deceived'."

Hesemann, apparently taking it all very seriously, was on this
occasion responding to comments raised at a MUFON conference and
which supposedly came from one of Billy Meier's ET contacts, a
'Plejaran called Ptaah', who claimed Hesemann worked with too
many charlatans, was easily fooled and also believed that he
[Hesemann] might be an alien.

Hesemann is of course a well-known promoter of Meier's flying
saucer photographs/contactee tales and defender of their
legitimacy.

It's this typical background which ensures that skepticism will
never owe ufology any apologies.


Starved and devoid of the proof it so craves, the campaign for
acceptance of alien visitation reality - it used to be called
'ufology', I think it's now known as the 'Disclosure Project' -
forcibly resorts to anecdotes. Any fantasy which emerges when
'hypnotised' can be declared corroborative evidence.

Not that I would wish to offend any self-professed 'me too'
abductees, as they might hit me with their handbags.

And that's just the guys!


The telling feedback from my 'Fortean Times' article came via
objective researchers and informed case historians such as Robert
Sheaffer, not Adamski or Gulf Breeze, etc. devotees. It was also
welcome to receive an endorsement from Martin Kottmeyer, whose
earlier research I had built on.

Amongst the most significant endorsements were comments expressed
by Dr Jacqueline Mitton, Public Relations Officer for the Royal
Astronomical Society these past 13 years or so.

Dr Mitton wrote, "I found what you had to say of great interest
and your detailed research adds strong weight to the
interpretation of Arnold's sighting as birds".

Dr Mitton considered that my research, particularly the profound
repercussions resulting from an almost certain identification of
'Arnold's peak', merited being presented to the 'British
Association for the Advancement of Science'.

Apropos disenchantment from Bennett and his ilk, I would have to
be comfortable with such peer review from somewhat more
scientific sources, not all of which I can publish, at present.


Those who, like Bennett, perceive 'anarcho-mystical skepticism',
whatever that's supposed to be, as 'a nasty virus' can doubtless
find solace in the usual ravings on 'Plejaran UpDates'...
whatever.

Perhaps subscribers who also advocate 'flying saucers' and 'alien
abductions' to be 'real', can explain how a demonstrably default
skepticism of same draws a comparison to "the prisons and
concentration camps of Stalin and Hitler".


I'm reminded of an apposite quote on Robert Sheaffer's web site
[www.debunker.com]:

"Anyone who suggests that UFOs are anything but alien spacecraft
soon finds out how it feels to be taken apart by a pack of flesh-
ripping religious weasels."

Peter Brookesmith, Fortean Times, May, 2000.


Fortunately, they're effectively toothless; always have been and
on current form, always will be.

From: voyager@ukonline.co.uk
X-Originating-IP: 172.183.78.195
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2002 23:59:17 +0100 (BST)
Subject: [UFORL] Re: Bentwaters/Woodbridge UFOs

On the question of 'trained observers' being deceived by
planets/stars, Dr. Donald H. Menzel had this to say in a prepared
paper for the 'Symposium on Unidentified Flying Objects', July
29, 1968:

[...]

Nevertheless, the UFO buffs believe, almost as an article of
faith, that "trained observers," such as military or airline
pilots, could not possibly mistake a meteor, a planet, a star, a
sundog, or a mirage for a UFO. This viewpoint is absolutely
nonsense and the Air Force files bear witness to its falsity!
They contain thousands of solved cases -- sightings by "reliable
individuals" like the pilots: But such persons have made huge
errors in identification.

A huge meteor flashes in the sky! The co-pilot thinks it is going
to strike the plane and takes evasive action. The pilot disagrees
and he is right. The UFO proves to be a fireball or meteor a
hundred miles away! Such occurrences are frequent, not rare. They
have even increased with the growing number of re-entries and
spectacular decay of satellite debris from the space operations
of the U.S.A. and the U.S.S.R.

Distances overhead are uncommonly hard to estimate -- either on
the ground or in the air. A bird's feather, shining brightly in
the sun and floating a mere 20 feet overhead may seem to be a
distant object moving at very high speed. Conversely, a pilot may
think that a bright object on the horizon, in reality a star or
planet, lies just beyond his wing tip. Sometimes, a layer of warm
air, sandwiched between 2 layers of cold air, can act as a lens,
projecting a pulsing, spinning, vividly colored, saucer-like
image of a planet. Pilots, thinking they were dealing with a
nearby flying object, have often tried to intercept the image,
which evades all attempts to cut it off. The distance may seem to
change rapidly, as the star fades or increases in brightness.
Actual "dog fights" have been recorded between a confused
military pilot and a planet. I myself have observed this
phenomenon of star mirage. It is both realistic and frightening.

Such observations fortified the UFO legend -- that these objects
"maneuver as if under intelligent control." But the pilots failed
to realize that the "intelligent control" came from within
themselves. And I think that Air Force personnel of Project Blue
Book still do not appreciate this important UFO phenomenon.
Mirages are not the only apparitions that appear to maneuver. I
think I was the first person, to point out that a special kind of
reflection of the sun (or moon), sometimes called a sun dog (or
moon dog), also can perform evasive action. Layers of ice
crystals are necessary, like those found in cirrus clouds. An
aviator flying through cirrus sometimes sees a peculiar metallic
appearing reflection, a reflection of the sun or moon. He may
elect to chase it. The apparition will recede if approached, or
approach if the pilot reverses his course. The object seems to
execute evasive action! As the pilot runs out of ice crystals,
the UFO will seem to put on a burst of speed and disappear into
the distance.

But such behavior does not imply, as the UFO addicts argue, the
presence of an intelligent pilot to guide it. No! It's like
chasing a rainbow, which recedes as you approach it or advances
as you move away.

As we look over the Air Force files, we find that some 90 per
cent of the solved cases result from the presence of material
objects in the atmosphere. I list some of these objects.
Reflections from airplanes, banking in the sun, simulate saucers.
Momentarily, a bright reflection appears and then vanishes. The
plane is invisible in the distant haze. An imaginative person
concludes that an interplanetary vehicle has come in fast,
reversed course, and rapidly receded into the distance. Often the
observers say "It couldn't have been a plane," because "no noise
was heard" or because "it moved too swiftly." And yet careful
study proves beyond doubt that the object was indeed an aircraft.
The brilliant landing lights of a plane can almost dazzle a
person on the ground. Sometimes such lights may appear to be very
close -- only a few hundred feet away.

You'd be surprised at the variety of mundane objects that people
have reported as UFO's. Balloons, child's balloons, weather
balloons lighted or unlighted, and especially those enormous
plastic balloons as large as a ten-story building, which carry
scientific instruments to altitudes of 100,000 feet! Reflecting
full sunlight while the earth below lies in dim twilight, these
balloons shine more-brilliantly than Venus! Advertising planes or
illuminated blimps frequently become UFO's.

Birds, by day or night, often reflect light from their shiny
backs. Windblown kites, hats, paper, plastic sacks, feathers,
spider-webs, seed pods, dust devils have all contributed their
share of UFO sightings. Insects single or in swarms. Saucer-
shaped clouds, reflections of searchlights on clouds! Special
space experiments, such as rocket-launched sodium vapor releases
or balloons from Wallop's Island have also produced spectacular
apparitions! Ball lightning and the Aurora Borealis occasionally
contribute.

Reflections from power lines, insulators, television antennas,
radars, radio telescopes, even apartment windows! These, too,
have produced realistic UFO's.

I could add to this list almost indefinitely. But the chief point
I want to make is that simple phenomena like the above have
tricked intelligent people into reporting a UFO.

[...]

On our return across Minnesota we had an experience which I have
always remembered as illustrative of the fallacy of all human
testimony about ghosts, rappings, and other phenomena of that
character. We spent two nights and a day at Fort Snelling. Some
of the officers were greatly surprised by a celestial phenomenon
of a very extraordinary character which had been observed for
several nights past. A star had been seen, night after night,
rising in the east as usual, and starting on its course toward
the south. But instead of continuing that course across the
meridian, as stars invariably had done from the remotest
antiquity, it took a turn toward the north, sunk toward the
horizon, and finally set near the north point of the horizon. Of
course an explanation was wanted.

My assurance that there must be some mistake in the observation
could not be accepted, because this erratic course of the
heavenly body had been seen by all of them so plainly that no
doubt could exist on the subject. The men who saw it were not of
the ordinary untrained kind, but graduates of West Point, who, if
any one, ought to be free from optical deceptions. I was
confidently invited to look out that night and see for myself. We
all watched with the greatest interest.

In due time the planet Mars was seen in the east making its way
toward the south. "There it is!" was the exclamation.

"Yes, there it is," said I. "Now that planet is going to keep
right on its course toward the south."

"No, it is not," said they; "you will see it turn around and go
down towards the north."

Hour after hour passed, and as the planet went on its regular
course, the other watchers began to get a little nervous. It
showed no signs of deviating from its course. We went out from
time to time to look at the sky.
"There it is," said one of the observers at length, pointing to
Capella, which was now just rising a little to the east of north;
"there is the star setting."

"No, it isn't," said I; "there is the star we have been looking
at, now quite inconspicuous near the meridian, and that star
which you think is setting is really rising and will soon be
higher up."

A very little additional watching showed that no deviation of the
general laws of Nature had occurred, but that the observers of
previous nights had jumped at the conclusion that two objects,
widely apart in the heavens, were the same.

Those words came from a book called "Reminiscences of an
Astronomer," published in 1903 by Simon Newcomb, who was in
charge of the American Nautical Almanac office from 1877 until
1897. The event actually occurred in 1866. The similarity to
modern UFO's is overpowering. A star cavorting across the sky!
Military officers as responsible witnesses!
[END]


The full text is online, courtesy of the 'National Capital Area
Skeptics', at:

http://912a-87.umd.edu/ufosymposium/menzel.html


James Easton.
E-mail: voyager@ufoworld.co.uk
www.ufoworld.co.uk

I am an indirect witness to this. On 10/16/1973, my city was in the
midst of a rash of UFO sightings. I decided to go out that evening and
see if I could find out what was going on. I found a location which gave
me a clear view of the entire sky, with only a small obstruction to the
west in a distant row of trees.

I observed from 7 pm until 12 pm, EST. I saw one meteor, two
airplanes, some stars, and Mars glowing brilliantly in the east. Mars
was at opposition, and was brighter than it was last year. But not one
UFO showed up. I took reference photos of Mars and of one of the
planes.

The next day, I waited for the papers to come, to see if any UFOs
had been reported. There was a rash of sightings that night. There
were two groups of sightings with different characteristics:

1. One group of people several miles west of my location reported
that a low flying UFO had come from the northwest, passed
overhead, and disappeared in the southeast.

That same day, the paper also reported that the remains of a fire
balloon had been found on Rockport Road, about where the UFO
had disappeared.

2. Two other groups of people about 2 miles west of me reported a
stationary UFO which seemed to them to be hovering right over my
position. Since I didn't see it, it must have been either something
very close to where they were and below my horizon, or Mars, which
was in the right direction, but way beyond my position.

@ CONDON REPORT - CASE 37.

@ An interesting case to reference Tim.

@ Can you explain to me Tim how the radar confirmation is
@ conveniently killed off.

There is an interesting phenomenon in UFO sightings. I like to
call it "told where to look".

Most laymen think of RADAR as being a kind of TV picture of what
is in the air. With transponders on all planes, this is generally true.
But in 1967, only a few military and commercial flights had
transponders. Everything else in the air was just a blip. Adding to
the confusion, there were also blips which did NOT correspond to
something known to be in the air - all of the time, not just during
UFO sightings. Which is why RADAR now has transponders on all
aircraft - the spurious blips (including stray UFOs) will no longer
show on the screen.

If a RADAR operator was asked to find a target in a specific direction
or area in the days before universal transponders, he would inevitably
find one of those spurious blips, and tell the person calling that he had
something there.

The spurious blips were eventually traced to several different causes:

- Ground objects high enough to reflect the beam back.
- Multipath interference, where the beam can bounce off of two or more
   objects in sequence.
- Corner reflectors on the ground. One operator was able to tell a
   construction company owner where all of his dump trucks were.
- Second pulse (or second trip) echoes. These are echoes from
   objects so far away that the RADAR set had already sent out a
   new pulse. The distance was computed from the new pulse, not
   the old one.
- Gremlins within the RADAR set itself. Usually these involved
   standing waves in the mercury delay line used to implement
   devices which reject stationary targets.

@ And when was the last time you read your wrist watch
@ under the glow/light of Venus? Again some very strange
@ physics here folks.

Oh really? I guess you have never been far enough away from
electric lights for your scotopic (night) vision to switch itself on.
It takes about 15 minutes of being in a very dark environment,
devoid of artificial light and with no moon, before scotopic vision
begins to work.

That is how long it takes the rod cells in your eye to replace the
visual purple pigment (rhodopsin), which is bleached out and
rendered useless by brighter light. Simultaneously, your irises
have opened to the largest aperture. And then, after that 15
minute wait, the visual purple increases the gain of the rod cells,
and you can see with very little light, in black and white vision.

After my scotopic vision has come on, I can read a large dial
watch with thick hands. Digital watches are too small to be read,
because scotopic acuity is not as good as photopic (day) acuity.
And you have to look slightly to one side of the watch, because
the fovea has no rod cells in it. The center of your scotopic vision
becomes blurred as a result.

This does not work on a solidly overcast night with no source of
light at all, unless a distant city provides enough light. Starlight
is enough to illuminate things, but not a totally dark environment.

Try it! It works! But one look at a distant auto headlight and you
have to start the waiting period over. Looking at stars does not
restart the period. But Venus appears almost dazzling with full
scotopic vision.

During World War II, many military devices were made with dim
red illumination, because red light does not bleach out the visual
purple. Men were trained in dark-adaptation, so they would not
accidentally wipe out their scotopic vision. Light one cigarette,
and it's gone.

This is also why it hurts when someone comes into your room
at night while you are sleeping and turns on the light. With the
gain cranked all the way up, your eyes are overloaded.

Some people have reported this ordinary phenomenon of human
vision to me as though they had experienced some kind of
paranormal experience. In each case, it was the first time the
person had been away from artificial light. And in each case, they
were astonished when I told them that almost all humans can do
this (but a vitamin A deficiency prevents it from working).

@ The big question always left out in discussions related to stars

You turn up the gain of the eye.

The above phenomenon, witnessed for the first time, is that
striking. But since most people are never away from artificial
light, they never get to use it. On the other hand, if you know how
to use it, it comes in handy.
